DecSummary: The worker broke his left wrist/hand at work in December 2002. He had completed most of a college degree in electrical engineering technology and had done prior work terms with the employer, although was not on a college sponsored work term at the time of the accident. He injured his knee in October 2003 while doing electrical installation work for the same employer. While there had been discussions about the employer sponsoring the worker for his apprenticeship, he was formally sponsored by another company in November 2003. In a June 2004 decision, the Board determined that he was not an apprentice at the time of the hand injury in 2002. The worker's LOE benefits continued to be paid under his wrist claim even after his knee injury. He appealed ARO decisions regarding the earnings basis for his 2003 knee injury, denying an extension of time to object to the June 2004 decision, denying reimbursement for taxi expenses and supplies for his LMR activities, and denying entitlement for medical marijuana.
